bluf: Harbingers is a Kraków based Polish digital agency, self styled #Gamechangers, pairing young company energy with a 15+ years experience claim across paid media, SEO and content, selling to a mixed B2B and ecommerce base. It is doing productised GEO: a prepaid AI Overview & GEO readiness audit sold through Stripe, two 2026-2030 playbooks, a 2025 AI-Driven Marketing conference and five European Paid Media Awards 2026 finalist nominations. Horus reads it Neutral at +8, best placed for KJ1 and most exposed to KJ4. A rival should know: the record names not one client, the homepage served the crawler a bot verification page, and it sells AI visibility with no llms.txt.

What the base needs next is therefore inferred from the sold mix. Read against KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer), the paid media clients behind the nominations are likely to see their execution hours absorbed, and the record shows no first party data or measurement depth to hold them; that is a judgment on the mix, not on any named client.

openings:
The strongest opening is the empty book. The record names no client, no case study and no channel mix behind five award nominations; a rival with named, described work is very likely, at moderate confidence, to out evidence Harbingers, whose proof is nominations and a blog. The falsifier: a recompile past the bot verification page that surfaces a client wall or case studies.

The contradiction to lead with: it sells an AI Overview & GEO readiness audit and publishes no llms.txt on a site with 34 AI-topic URLs. The exposure to press is KJ4: paid search and paid social hours with no first party data, creative volume or measurement depth in the record (P4 partial), no test of ads inside assistants (P8 absent) and no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent). The offer that undercuts is an audited AI visibility number plus the machine readable layer, priced as a product the way Harbingers already prices; because P5 is making, a rival must beat it on proof, not price transparency. Monsoon (displacement 59.5) says the book likely buys on price, so a cheaper productised audit is roughly as likely to win as a better one.
